speaker: Unknown
en: So this episode is going to be a little different.
zh: 所以这一集会有点不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not on a book, but it's on this excellent long form profile of Mark Zuckerberg that my friend Jeremy Stern wrote.
zh: 这不是关于一本书的，而是关于我朋友 Jeremy Stern 写的一篇关于 Mark Zuckerberg 的精彩长篇人物特写。

speaker: Unknown
en: The name of the profile, the title of the profile is called Mark, and the subtitle is A Journey to the Heart of History's Largest Non-Territorial Empire.
zh: 这篇特写的名字，标题叫做《Mark》,副标题是《通往历史上最大的非领土帝国核心之旅》。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the piece opens with Jeremy interviewing Mark Zuckerberg's parents.
zh: 文章开头是 Jeremy 采访 Mark Zuckerberg 的父母。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he says, there they are, the Zuckerbergs.
zh: 他说：他们来了，Zuckerberg 一家。

speaker: Unknown
en: They look you in the eye and they don't break contact.
zh: 他们直视你的眼睛，不会移开视线。

speaker: Unknown
en: His dad is a ham.
zh: 他爸爸是个爱表演的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: His mother is shy.
zh: 他妈妈很害羞。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know what I expected them to be like, but for whatever reason, this wasn't it.
zh: 我不知道我原本以为他们会是什么样，但不知为什么，不是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they talk about what Mark was like as a child.
zh: 于是他们聊起 Mark 小时候是什么样。

speaker: Unknown
en: His dad says, he didn't stand out as the bright one in the family.
zh: 他爸爸说：他在家里并不显得特别聪明。

speaker: Unknown
en: If anyone, I would guess our middle daughter, Donna, was considered the nerd or the smart one in the family.
zh: 如果非要说的话，我猜我们的二女儿 Donna 才被认为是家里的书呆子或者最聪明的一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: His dad continues, we just had four really bright, successful kids.
zh: 他爸爸接着说：我们就是有四个非常聪明、成功的孩子。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're equally proud of all of them.
zh: 我们对他们都同样骄傲。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mark just happened to be in the right place at the right time.
zh: Mark 只是碰巧在正确的时间出现在了正确的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was a perfect confluence of his passion.
zh: 那是他的热情完美交汇的结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then his mom,
zh: 然后他妈妈，

speaker: Unknown
en: Hits on something that you and I talk about over and over again.
zh: 说到了你和我反复谈论的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: You see this in these biographies that you and I talk about.
zh: 你在你和我聊过的这些传记里都能看到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And usually there's some kind of passion or interest that they have.
zh: 通常他们都有某种热情或兴趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: True interest is revealed early, usually in childhood.
zh: 真正的兴趣很早就显露出来，通常是在童年。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so his mom says, I think people who have a passion are the luckiest people in the world.
zh: 所以他妈妈说：我认为有热情的人是世界上最幸运的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so then Jeremy asks Zuck's parents, were there signs?
zh: 然后 Jeremy 问 Zuck 的父母：有迹象吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And says, yes, perhaps there were some.
zh: 然后说：是的，也许有一些。

speaker: Unknown
en: In nursery school, he became so possessed by a one-week unit on outer space that he employed the teacher to extend the unit to a month.
zh: 在幼儿园的时候，他被一个为期一周的外太空主题单元迷住了，以至于他让老师把这个单元延长到一个月。

speaker: Unknown
en: To which she relented at the insistence of a four-year-old.
zh: 老师在一个四岁孩子的坚持下让步了。

speaker: Unknown
en: By the time he was six, his incessant demands for logical explanations of rules and step-by-step justifications for consequences that he expected his parents to prepare before laying down the law.
zh: 到他六岁的时候，他不断要求对规则给出合乎逻辑的解释、对后果给出一步步的论证，他期望父母在立规矩之前先准备好这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was this habit that Zuck had when he was six that they thought he was actually gonna become a lawyer.
zh: 正是 Zuck 六岁时的这个习惯，让他们以为他真的会成为一名律师。

speaker: Unknown
en: So by the time he was 12, he's already writing computer programs, he's building games.
zh: 所以到他 12 岁的时候，他已经在写电脑程序了，他在做游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's also this time when he was 12 and a virus crashed, the computer game he'd built, but he did not back up.
zh: 还有这么一件事，他 12 岁时，一次病毒崩溃了他做的电脑游戏，但他没有备份。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was devastated and he declared through tears that not only would he rebuild the game from scratch, but he'd find new ways to optimize it.
zh: 他崩溃了，他流着泪宣称，他不仅要从头重建这个游戏，还要找到新的方法来优化它。

speaker: Unknown
en: He'd make the game better and faster this time and God damn it, he would never forget to back up his work again.
zh: 这次他要把游戏做得更好更快，而且该死的，他再也不会忘记备份他的作品了。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is also one of the most fascinating parts about the story is it gets into Zuck's kind of fascination or maybe even obsession with the Roman Empire and with Augustus.
zh: 这个故事还有一个最迷人的部分，就是它讲到了 Zuck 对罗马帝国的着迷，或者甚至可以说是痴迷，以及对 Augustus 的痴迷。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this game when he was 12 says the game was set in the Roman Empire.
zh: 所以他 12 岁时做的这个游戏，文章说，游戏设定在罗马帝国。

speaker: Unknown
en: The player would conquer the world one territory at a time.
zh: 玩家要一个疆域一个疆域地征服世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: Perhaps that was a sign too.
zh: 也许那也是一个迹象。

speaker: Unknown
en: This through line continues.
zh: 这条贯穿线还在延续。

speaker: Unknown
en: In high school, he excelled at Latin.
zh: 高中时，他拉丁语很出色。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nearly a decade later, he still recalled the Latin verse for Jupiter's Decree in the Ennead.
zh: 将近十年之后，他仍然记得《Ennead》中 Jupiter 法令的拉丁语诗句。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is the quote.
zh: 这句诗是：

speaker: Unknown
en: For these, I set no bounds in space or time.
zh: 「为他们，我在空间或时间上不设界限，

speaker: Unknown
en: I have given empire without end.
zh: 我已赐予无尽的帝国。」

speaker: Unknown
en: At Harvard, one of the first websites that Mark built was a class study tool for the art history course called Rome of Augustus.
zh: 在哈佛，Mark 最早建立的网站之一是一门名为《Augustus 的罗马》的艺术史课程的学习工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: At early crisis Facebook meetings to fend off threats from Google, Mark would end his speeches by declaring, Carthage must be destroyed.
zh: 在早期的 Facebook 危机会议上，为了抵御来自 Google 的威胁，Mark 会以宣告「迦太基必须被毁灭」来结束他的演讲。

speaker: Unknown
en: All hands meetings would end with him shouting domination.
zh: 全员会议会以他高喊「统治」结束。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sean Parker, Facebook's early president, warned Mark that shouting domination could one day be cited in an antitrust suit, and Sean Parker later observed that Zuck had this kind of imperial tendency in him.
zh: Facebook 的早期总裁 Sean Parker 警告 Mark,高喊「统治」有朝一日可能在反垄断诉讼中被引用，而且 Sean Parker 后来评价说 Zuck 身上有这种帝国式的倾向。

speaker: Unknown
en: In more recent years, Zuck periodically mused in public about the really harsh approach Augustus employed before establishing 200 years of world peace.
zh: 近年来，Zuck 不时在公开场合沉思，谈起 Augustus 在建立 200 年世界和平之前所采用的非常严厉的手段。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a direct quote from Mark.
zh: 这是 Mark 的一句直接引语。

speaker: Unknown
en: That didn't come for free.
zh: 那不是白白得来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's talking about Rome's first emperor who turned it from a republic into an empire.
zh: 他说的是罗马的第一位皇帝，他把罗马从共和国变成了帝国。

speaker: Unknown
en: He had to do certain things, Mark said.
zh: 他必须做一些特定的事情，Mark 说。

speaker: Unknown
en: At the company's flagship annual conference in 2024, Mark wore a shirt with the words, either a Caesar or nothing.
zh: 在 2024 年公司的旗舰年度大会上，Mark 穿着一件衬衫，上面写着：要么是凯撒，要么什么都不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mark's wife Priscilla Chan joked that on their honeymoon in Rome, his constant pursuit of Augustian sights and statues made the emperor their third wheel.
zh: Mark 的妻子 Priscilla Chan 开玩笑说，在罗马度蜜月时，他对奥古斯都时期景点和雕像的执着追寻，让这位皇帝成了他们的电灯泡。

speaker: Unknown
en: The names of their three children are Maxima, August, and Aurelia.
zh: 他们三个孩子的名字分别是 Maxima、August 和 Aurelia。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so Jeremy Stern is a fantastic writer because he's going back.
zh: 所以 Jeremy Stern 是一位出色的作者，因为他会往回追溯。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it starts with him interviewing the parents.
zh: 所以文章一开始是他采访 Mark 的父母。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then he goes into Mark's fascination with Augustus, and he brings, he weaves this, he does this constantly throughout the piece in all his pieces.
zh: 然后他深入讲 Mark 对奥古斯都的痴迷，他把这些编织进来，他在整篇文章里不断地这样做，在他所有的文章里都是如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: Highly recommend reading all the pieces he's writing on entrepreneurs and investors these days.
zh: 强烈推荐去读他最近写的所有关于创业者和投资人的文章。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think he is the best in the world at what he's doing right now.
zh: 我认为他是这个领域当今世界上做得最好的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what he does back here is like, we start with talking about interviewing Mark's parents, then we go into this fascination with Augustus, then he brings it back into, you almost forget, the storytelling is so amazing in this piece, you almost forget that where we are, we're actually in a conversation with Mark Zuckerberg's parents.
zh: 但他在这里所做的是，比如，我们从采访 Mark 的父母开始，然后深入讲他对奥古斯都的痴迷，然后他又把话题拉回来，你几乎会忘记，这篇文章的叙事太精彩了，你几乎忘了我们现在身处何处——其实我们是在和 Mark Zuckerberg 的父母对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so he says, this is the question that I came here to ask.
zh: 于是他说，这就是我来这里要问的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is it like for one of the most powerful men in human history who better or for worse has by age 42 secured a place in the books that'll be written about his era for centuries after his death to be your child?
zh: 对于人类历史上最有权势的人之一——无论好坏，他在 42 岁时就已经确保了自己在关于这个时代的史书中的地位，这些书在他死后还将流传几个世纪——这样一个人的孩子是什么感受？

speaker: Unknown
en: And this goes on for quite some time, but I want to pull out some of my favorite highlights here.
zh: 这段内容持续了相当长的时间，但我想摘出一些我最喜欢的亮点。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's complicated, his mom says.
zh: 这很复杂，他妈妈说。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very, very complicated, his father agrees, but he knows what people need and want, sometimes even before they know it.
zh: 非常非常复杂，他父亲表示同意，但他知道人们需要什么、想要什么，有时甚至在他们自己知道之前。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, people call him arrogant.
zh: 我是说，有人称他傲慢。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's not.
zh: 他不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: But time after time, his arrogance just turns into truth.
zh: 但一次又一次，他的傲慢最终都变成了事实。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there's this excellent line that anybody with kids will understand.
zh: 然后还有一句极好的话，任何有孩子的人都会懂。

speaker: Unknown
en: Zuck's dad says, you will experience it one day too, when your children eclipse you.
zh: Zuck 的爸爸说：等你有一天被你的孩子超越时，你也会体会到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Karen nods and waits for her husband to finish, then she comes alive.
zh: Karen 点点头，等她丈夫说完，然后她来了精神。

speaker: Unknown
en: She shifts her posture back towards me with a tender but firm gaze.
zh: 她调整姿势重新转向我，目光温柔而坚定。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can tell you how it is for me as a mother.
zh: 我可以告诉你，作为一位母亲，这对我来说是怎样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is my child.
zh: 这是我的孩子。

speaker: Unknown
en: The eye of Sauron is how her child's longtime lieutenants have referred to the unblinking, sometimes unnerving silences he involuntarily imposes when preparing to answer a question or make a point.
zh: 「索伦之眼」——这是她孩子的资深副手们用来形容他那种不由自主的、不眨眼的沉默的称呼，有时令人不安，那是在他准备回答一个问题或阐述一个观点时会出现的沉默。

speaker: Unknown
en: I see it now, I think.
zh: 我想，我现在见识到了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So she continues.
zh: 于是她继续说。

speaker: Unknown
en: Things have been written and said about him that are so untrue from such an early age.
zh: 从他很早的时候起，就有太多关于他的文字和言论如此不真实。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wish that sometimes the people who do that would reflect on what it must be like to fabricate stories or create their own imaginary scenarios of what this person is like.
zh: 我希望有时那些做这些事的人能反思一下：编造故事、虚构自己对这个人是什么样的想象场景，那会是一种什么感受。

speaker: Unknown
en: I sometimes really wonder if anyone has ever sat back and thought, this is a real person.
zh: 我有时真的想知道，是否有人曾静下心想一想：这是一个真实的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: It has been really brutal, she says.
zh: 这一直非常残酷，她说。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, how would you feel if your child was subjected to this kind of scrutiny?
zh: 我是说，如果你的孩子受到这种审视，你会作何感受？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so Jeremy asked to follow up, do you wish he'd stop?
zh: 于是 Jeremy 追问道：你希望他停下来吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And his mother responds, I always said to him, just do this only as long as you can find happiness within it.
zh: 他的母亲回答说：我总是对他说，只要你能从中找到快乐，就继续做下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: It has to bring you joy.
zh: 它必须带给你快乐。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of my favorite parts in the piece that comes later is Mark emphatically says, I will never stop.
zh: 文章后面我最喜欢的部分之一是 Mark 明确地说：我永远不会停下。

speaker: Unknown
en: So then the story transitions to another setting and it says, Mark Zuckerberg is suspended in midair by an NCAA Division I wrestling champion who is slamming him to the floor.
zh: 然后故事切换到另一个场景，写道：Mark Zuckerberg 被一位 NCAA 第一级别摔跤冠军悬吊在半空中，正把他摔向地面。

speaker: Unknown
en: Zuckerberg has spoken in public about his affinity for the masculine energy of MMA fighting as a counterbalance to the neutered or emasculated corporate world and America society writ large.
zh: Zuckerberg 曾在公开场合谈到他对 MMA 格斗那种男性气概力量的喜爱，以此作为对 neutered 或被阉割的企业世界乃至整个美国社会的对冲。

speaker: Unknown
en: He decided to give up his lifelong habit of sleeping in late in order to hit people and get hit three mornings a week.
zh: 他决定放弃自己睡懒觉的终身习惯，以便每周有三个早晨可以去打人和挨打。

speaker: Unknown
en: says for 23 years, the single fact dominating every moment of every room he's been in is that he is Mark Zuckerberg.
zh: 写道，23 年来，他所处的每一个房间的每一刻都有一个压倒一切的事实，那就是他是 Mark Zuckerberg。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's been true, not just at Meta, but in his congressional testimonies and court proceedings, at Taylor Swift concerts and the Prada runway show at the Milan Fashion Week, at dinners with friends and birthday parties of his daughter's friends.
zh: 这一直如此，不仅在 Meta，在他的国会听证会和法庭程序上，在 Taylor Swift 的演唱会和米兰时装周的 Prada 走秀上，在与朋友的晚餐和他女儿朋友的生日派对上。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's been true even in his meetings with heads of state, including his own commander in chief, to whom it must occur as they've tried at various points to squeeze and threaten and blame him for everything from electoral outcomes to ethnic cleansings.
zh: 即便在他与国家元首的会面中，包括与他自己的三军统帅的会面中，这也一直如此。而对他们来说，在他们多次试图挤压他、威胁他、把从选举结果到种族清洗的一切都归咎于他的时候，这一点必然会浮现：

speaker: Unknown
en: that one day they will be out of office, and eventually dead, while Zuckerberg, whose majority control of Meta's voting power makes his removal effectively impossible, could in 50 years still be ruler of his empire.
zh: 那就是有一天他们会下台，最终死去，而 Zuckerberg——他对 Meta 投票权的多数控制使他被移除实际上不可能——在 50 年后仍可能是他帝国的统治者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today, that empire has 3.6 billion users and a market cap of 1.6 trillion dollars.
zh: 今天，这个帝国拥有 36 亿用户和 1.6 万亿美元的市值。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is not a normal situation for a human being to be in, let alone from the time they are 19 years old.
zh: 一个人处于这样的境地绝非正常，更不用说从 19 岁起就是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: 300,000 years of evolutionary biology do not furnish a man in this position with the keys to easily access other people or reality.
zh: 30 万年的进化生物学并没有赋予处于这种位置的人轻松接近他人或现实的钥匙。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yet for all the ways in which Zuckerberg's life is statistically anomalous, the conundrum he's in is ancient.
zh: 然而，尽管 Zuckerberg 的生活在统计上如此反常，他所处的困境却由来已久。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the conundrum they're referring to is the dictator's dilemma.
zh: 而他们所指的困境就是独裁者的困境。

speaker: Unknown
en: The idea is simple and intuitive.
zh: 这个概念简单而直观。

speaker: Unknown
en: The more power a man acquires, the more his empire expands, the more he depends on other people for information about everything, from his own court to the furthest reaches of the empire.
zh: 一个人获取的权力越多，他的帝国扩张得越大，他就越依赖其他人来获取关于一切的信息，从他自己的宫廷到帝国最遥远的疆域。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yet through fear or awe or self-preservation, those people often become less willing to tell him what they think he doesn't want to hear, leaving him increasingly insulated from reality even as the consequences of his decisions become larger and as the barriers to believing one's own bullshit fall away.
zh: 然而由于恐惧、敬畏或自我保护，这些人往往变得不太愿意告诉他那些他认为不想听的话，使他越来越与现实隔绝，与此同时他的决策所造成的后果却越来越大，而相信自己胡说八道的门槛也在不断降低。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there's some great historical examples of this dictator's dilemma.
zh: 关于这种独裁者困境，历史上有一些很好的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thus, in the spring of 1941, there were no officers left with the courage to implore Stalin after he scoffed at the intelligence that a German invasion was coming.
zh: 因此,到了1941年春天,在斯大林嘲笑了关于德国入侵即将到来的情报之后,再也没有军官有勇气去恳求他了。

speaker: Unknown
en: For three years, the Great Leap Forward's mass famines were reported up to Mao as record harvests.

speaker: Unknown
en: It was the self-censorship of JFK's advisors during deliberations on the Bay of Pigs that popularized the term groupthink.
zh: 正是肯尼迪(JFK)的顾问们在猪湾事件商议过程中的自我审查，使得「群体思维」这个词流行开来。

speaker: Unknown
en: The Shah of Iran was protected by his court from indications of a coming revolution until it was already too late.
zh: 伊朗国王被他的宫廷屏蔽了关于即将到来革命的种种迹象，直到为时已晚。

speaker: Unknown
en: Henry Ford ignored warnings that the Model T was dying until the market was dominated instead by General Motors.
zh: 亨利·福特无视关于 Model T 正在衰亡的警告，直到市场转而被通用汽车占据主导。

speaker: Unknown
en: Afraid of their volatile superiors, middle managers at Nokia in 2007 downplayed the appearance of the iPhone.
zh: 2007 年诺基亚的中层管理者由于惧怕喜怒无常的上司，淡化了对 iPhone 问世的重视。

speaker: Unknown
en: The list of great statesmen in many ways is a list of figures obsessed by the dictator's dilemma.
zh: 伟大政治家的名单，在很多方面就是一份被独裁者困境所困扰的人物的名单。

speaker: Unknown
en: Lincoln, for instance, installed himself in the War Department's telegraph office in order to read field dispatches raw as they came off the wire before subordinates could filter them.
zh: 例如，林肯把自己安置在战争部的电报室里，以便在电报一从线上传出来、下属还来不及过滤之前，就直接阅读原始的战地电文。

speaker: Unknown
en: Churchill retained the frank and combative Alan Brooke as his top military advisor and built a private statistical office whose job was to cross-check every ministry's report.
zh: 丘吉尔留用了坦率而好斗的 Alan Brooke 作为他的最高军事顾问，并设立了一个私人统计办公室，其职责是交叉核查每个部门的报告。

speaker: Unknown
en: Kennedy, who learned from the Bay of Pigs, absented himself from the National Security Council sessions during the Cuban Missile Crisis so that his personal magnificence wouldn't affect the debate.
zh: 肯尼迪从猪湾事件中吸取了教训，在古巴导弹危机期间故意不参加国家安全委员会的会议，以免他个人的权威影响辩论。

speaker: Unknown
en: Warren Buffett called Charlie Munger his abominable no man
zh: 沃伦·巴菲特称 Charlie Munger 为他那“可憎的说不者”。

speaker: Unknown
en: for the rate at which he vetoed his ideas, for which Buffet was ultimately grateful.
zh: 因为他否决那些想法的速度之快，Buffet 最终对此心怀感激。

speaker: Unknown
en: As emperor, Augustus called on senators at random to stifle premeditated remarks, periodically rotated his advisory council, and tolerated libel and jokes at his own expense.
zh: 作为皇帝，Augustus 随机召见元老院议员以压制事先排练好的发言，定期轮换他的顾问委员会，并容忍针对他本人的诽谤和玩笑。

speaker: Unknown
en: He ran three censuses of Roman citizens, kept his own ledger of the empire's legions and treasuries, and instituted Rome's first carrier carriage system so that, like Lincoln, he could interrogate a direct source of information before anyone could corrupt it.
zh: 他对罗马公民进行过三次人口普查，自己记录了一份关于帝国军团和国库的账册，并建立了罗马的第一个驿传马车系统，这样，就像 Lincoln 一样，他可以在任何人腐蚀信息之前向第一手信息来源进行质询。

speaker: Unknown
en: Augustus reigned for 40 years and died in his bed.
zh: Augustus 在位 40 年，死在床上。

speaker: Unknown
en: According to the nearly three dozen people I interviewed for this story, Zuckerberg is hyper-aware of the dilemma's potential, which is to say, paranoid.
zh: 根据我为这篇报道采访的近三十多人所说，Zuckerberg 对这种困境的可能性有着极强的意识，也就是说，偏执。

speaker: Unknown
en: He is a micromanager and a voracious consumer of data.
zh: 他是一个微管理者，也是一个如饥似渴的数据消费者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Aware that any chief's inner circle is most incentivized to act as courtiers, he frequently engages the direct reports of his direct reports and the subordinates of the report's reports.
zh: 他深知任何首领的核心圈子最有动机去充当朝臣，因此他经常与他的直接下属的直接下属，以及下属的下属交流。

speaker: Unknown
en: He is known for inviting outside experts and commentators to visit him and argue about his decisions.
zh: 他以邀请外部专家和评论员来访、就他的决定进行争论而闻名。

speaker: Unknown
en: He often accepts personal blame in public for the mistakes of others, perhaps in part because he accepts the reality of Meta, which they accept too.
zh: 他经常在公开场合为他人的错误承担个人责任，部分原因或许是他接受了 Meta 的现实，而其他人也接受这个现实。

speaker: Unknown
en: He is the company, and the company is him.
zh: 他就是公司，公司就是他。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before we get back into this, I want to tell you about the presenting sponsor of this podcast, Ramp.
zh: 在我们继续之前，我想向你介绍本播客的冠名赞助商 Ramp。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have been reading a lot about SpaceX lately.
zh: 我最近读了很多关于 SpaceX 的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: SpaceX is one of the most valuable businesses in the world, and one of the main themes in the history of SpaceX is constantly attacking and questioning your cost.
zh: SpaceX 是世界上最有价值的公司之一，而 SpaceX 历史上的一个主要主题就是不断地攻击和质疑你的成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ramp helps many of the most innovative businesses in the world do exactly that, and they do this by using first principles thinking.
zh: Ramp 帮助世界上许多最具创新性的公司正是这样做的，他们通过第一性原理思维来实现这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: The median company running on Ramp cuts their expenses by 5%.
zh: 在 Ramp 上运营的公司中位数公司将其开支削减了 5%。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one thing that SpaceX has demonstrated is that a religious dedication to controlling your costs helps increase revenue because you can pursue opportunities you couldn't otherwise.
zh: 而 SpaceX 已经证明的一件事是，对控制成本的虔诚投入有助于增加收入，因为你可以追求原本无法追求的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we see that in the RAMP data too.
zh: 我们在 Ramp 的数据中也看到了这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: The median company running on RAMP also grows their revenue by 16%.
zh: 在 Ramp 上运营的公司中位数公司其收入也增长了 16%。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when you're running your business on RAMP and your competitors are not, you have a massive...
zh: 所以当你在 Ramp 上运营你的公司而你的竞争对手没有时，你就拥有了一个巨大的……

speaker: Unknown
en: Ramp is the only platform designed to make your finance team faster and happier.
zh: Ramp 是唯一一个旨在让你的财务团队更快、更快乐的平台。

speaker: Unknown
en: Many of the top founders and CEOs that I know run their business on Ramp.
zh: 我认识的许多顶级创始人和 CEO 都在 Ramp 上运营他们的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: I run my business on Ramp and you should too.
zh: 我的公司就在 Ramp 上运营，你也应该这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Go to ramp.com today to learn how they can help your business save time, save money and grow revenue.
zh: 今天就去 ramp.com 了解他们如何帮助你的公司节省时间、节省金钱并增加收入。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is ramp.com.
zh: 网址是 ramp.com。

speaker: Unknown
en: Much of Zuckerberg's inner circle consists of people who have been with him for over 15 years, since before Facebook's IPO in 2012.
zh: Zuckerberg 的核心圈子大部分由那些跟随他超过 15 年的人组成，从 2012 年 Facebook IPO 之前就一直如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some were even around in 2006, when nearly all of Facebook's management team quit after Zuckerberg, who was only 22, rejected their pleas to take an offer from Yahoo to buy the company for a billion dollars, forever establishing a central tenet of the company's culture.
zh: 有些人甚至早在 2006 年就在了，当时 Facebook 几乎所有管理团队都辞职了，因为当时年仅 22 岁的 Zuckerberg 拒绝了他们提出的接受雅虎以十亿美元收购公司的请求，从此确立了公司文化的一个核心信条。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the face of opposition, Zuckerberg is right.
zh: 面对反对时，Zuckerberg 是对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Others are people who long ago came to terms with the fact that they cannot do what he does and that despite his many mistakes and missteps, he is in a class all by himself.
zh: 另一些人则是早就接受了这样的事实的人：他们无法做他所做的事，而且尽管他犯了许多错误和失误，他仍然是一个独一无二的存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: Many are men and women with lives and livelihoods they never dreamed of and they owe it all, all of it, to him.
zh: 其中有许多是拥有他们做梦也想不到的生活和生计的男男女女，而他们把这一切，所有的一切，都归功于他。

speaker: Unknown
en: They may simply be too grateful, men in his position have often worried, to attempt too frequently or stridently to play the role of rescuing him from the isolation of his position, from the consequences of letting his relationship to reality slip for even a moment.
zh: 处在他这种位置的人常常担心，他们可能只是太过感激，以致于不会太频繁或太尖锐地去尝试扮演把他从其处境的孤立中拯救出来的角色，不让他与现实的关系哪怕有一刻的滑落所带来的后果。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even if he is forever probing for ways to escape the dilemma.
zh: 即使他永远在探寻摆脱这一困境的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even when it means he will get punched in the face.
zh: 即使这意味着他会挨一记迎面重拳。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then this is what I meant earlier.
zh: 然后这就是我之前想说的意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, you start with this scene where, okay, we have Mark, he's in the air, he's being slammed, talks about his affinity and his love for MMA and for fighting and the fact that he's doing it every day, he wakes up.
zh: 就像是，你从这个场景开始，好，我们有 Mark，他在空中，他被摔倒了，谈到他对 MMA 和格斗的喜爱和热爱，以及他每天都在做这件事，他一醒来就练。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this says three times a week.
zh: 而这里写的是每周三次。

speaker: Unknown
en: I heard that he does it every day for two hours as soon as he wakes up.
zh: 我听说他每天一醒来就练两个小时。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then he brings us back into the scene.
zh: 但接着他又把我们带回那个场景。

speaker: Unknown
en: Jeremy Cern, the writer, brings us back into the scene.
zh: 作家 Jeremy Cern 把我们带回那个场景。

speaker: Unknown
en: He says, the bell rings.
zh: 他说,铃响了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the fighters reshuffle.
zh: 拳手们重新交错。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before the bell sounds, he lands an overhand right on Zuckerberg's chin.
zh: 在铃响之前,他一记摆拳打在 Zuckerberg 的下巴上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we talk to, we see Jeremy talking to Zuckerberg's MMA coach about like, okay, what is this fascination?
zh: 然后我们跟——我们看到 Jeremy 跟 Zuckerberg 的 MMA 教练聊,大概是,好吧,这种痴迷到底是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, what is, what do you think that Mark's getting out of this?
zh: 就是,你觉得 Mark 从这件事里得到了什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: He says, I think we all have a void in our lives and the lucky ones find something that fills that space to make us more optimal, to make us a better human being.
zh: 他说,我认为我们每个人的生活中都有一个空洞,而幸运的人会找到某种东西来填补那个空间,让我们更优化,让我们成为更好的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mark filled the void with fighting.
zh: Mark 用格斗填补了那个空洞。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think he does like the element of danger.
zh: 我觉得他确实喜欢那种危险的元素。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you go left when you should have went right, you will get punched in the face.
zh: 如果你该往右却往了左,你就会被一拳打在脸上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so then we get to Zuckerberg's example of this maxim that you and I have talked about many times.
zh: 接着我们来看 Zuckerberg 的这个例子,关于你我谈过很多次的那条准则。

speaker: Unknown
en: It appears over and over again in these biographies.
zh: 它在这些传记中一遍又一遍地出现。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think most of his case entrepreneurs are obsessed with control.
zh: 我认为他的大多数——他这类创业者都痴迷于控制。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maximus essentially control the land upon which your business is built.
zh: 这条准则本质上是:控制你的业务所立足的那块土地。

speaker: Unknown
en: If something is critical to your business, you want to control it.
zh: 如果某样东西对你的业务至关重要,你就会想去控制它。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the central tensions of, I think, Zuckerberg's career and obviously this piece is the fact that he doesn't actually hold the land upon which his empire is built.
zh: 我认为,Zuckerberg 的职业生涯以及显然这篇文章的核心张力之一,就是他实际上并不拥有他的帝国所立足的那块土地。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so Jeremy does a great job of describing that.
zh: Jeremy 在描述这一点上做得很出色。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is a truism that while Zuckerberg is sovereign within his imperial court, he's immune to control by shareholders or his board, he does not actually hold the empire's territory.
zh: 有一个自明之理:虽然 Zuckerberg 在他的帝国宫廷内是主权者,不受股东或董事会的控制,但他实际上并不持有这个帝国的领土。

speaker: Unknown
en: He did only once, back when Facebook was a desktop site on the open web.
zh: 他只拥有过一次,那是 Facebook 还是开放网络上的一个桌面网站的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when the smartphone appeared, he lost his ground and never gained it back.
zh: 但当智能手机出现时,他失去了他的地盘,而且再也没能夺回来。

speaker: Unknown
en: The early trauma of having nearly missed the switch to mobile apps.
zh: 那种差点错过向移动应用转型的早期创伤。

speaker: Unknown
en: Scrambling during the 2012 IPO to rebuild Facebook and its advertising business around a platform shift that he didn't see coming or initially understand has never left him.
zh: 2012 年 IPO 期间手忙脚乱地围绕一场他没预见到、起初也不理解的平台转型重建 Facebook 及其广告业务——这段经历从未离开过他。

speaker: Unknown
en: Although the Facebook app's eventual conquest of mobile more or less made Apple's App Store, the App Store in turn made Facebook.
zh: 虽然 Facebook 应用电竞——应用最终对移动端的征服多少成就了 Apple 的 App Store,而 App Store 反过来又成就了 Facebook。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is a great line.
zh: 这一句写得非常好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Zuckerberg does not like being made.
zh: 而 Zuckerberg 不喜欢「被成就」。

speaker: Unknown
en: Many of Zuckerberg's ventures ever since have been puzzling to outsiders.
zh: 从那以后,Zuckerberg 的许多 ventures 在外人看来都令人费解。

speaker: Unknown
en: These ventures can also be understood as attempted jailbreaks from Apple and other competitors, a determination to regain and hold his territory.
zh: 这些 ventures 也可以被理解为从 Apple 和其他竞争者手中越狱的尝试,一种夺回并守住他领土的决心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thus, over the last 15 years,
zh: 因此,在过去 15 年里,

speaker: Unknown
en: Zuckerberg explored building a Facebook phone.
zh: Zuckerberg 探索过打造一部 Facebook 手机。

speaker: Unknown
en: He tried to replace the Android home screen with Facebook Home.
zh: 他试图用 Facebook Home 替换 Android 的主屏幕。

speaker: Unknown
en: He launched the Internet.org and its free basic service to deliver Facebook through carrier deals in India and other markets where Apple barely existed.
zh: 他推出了 Internet.org 及其免费基础服务,通过运营商协议在印度和其他 Apple 几乎不存在市场,把 Facebook 送达用户。

speaker: Unknown
en: He tried building Libra, a cryptocurrency, to facilitate payments.
zh: 他尝试打造 Libra,一种加密货币,以促成支付。

speaker: Unknown
en: He bought Oculus VR in the hopes that virtual reality headsets would replace the smartphone the way smartphones replace personal computers.
zh: 他收购了 Oculus VR,希望虚拟现实头显能取代智能手机,就像智能手机取代个人电脑那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Each has been a tunnel Zuckerberg dug to escape the prison of his competitors.
zh: 每一个都是 Zuckerberg 为逃离竞争者监狱而挖的一条隧道。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there's this great quote from Zuckerberg himself.
zh: 然后还有这段来自 Zuckerberg 本人的精彩引言。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of my things for the next 10 or 15 years is I just want to make sure we can build the fundamental technology that we're going to be building social experiences on.
zh: 「在未来 10 到 15 年里,我的目标之一就是,我要确保我们能够打造出我们将来构建社交体验所依赖的基础技术。」

speaker: Unknown
en: He told Jensen Wong at a conference in 2024 in the course of explaining his investment in building foundational AI models.
zh: 他在 2024 年的一场大会上告诉 Jensen Wong,当时他正在解释他投资打造基础 AI 模型这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Back to this direct quote from Zuck.
zh: 再回到 Zuck 的这段直接引述。

speaker: Unknown
en: There have been too many things that I've tried to build and then have been told, nah, you can't really build that by the platform provider.
zh: 「有太多东西是我尝试去打造、然后被告知,不,你其实不能打造那个,被平台提供方这么告知。」

speaker: Unknown
en: At some level, I'm just like, nah, fuck that.
zh: 「在某种程度上,我就是,不,去他妈的。」

speaker: Unknown
en: End of the quote by Zuckerberg and back to this fact that he is a singular lived experience.
zh: Zuckerberg 的引言到此结束,回到这个事实:他是一个独一无二的亲历者。

speaker: Unknown
en: I got to spend a few days with Zuck and one of the things I told him that I want him to do is come on the new show.
zh: 我曾和 Zuck 相处过几天,我告诉他的一件我希望他去做的事,就是来上我们的新节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was like, listen.
zh: 我当时说,听着。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have a singular experience.
zh: 你有一段独一无二的经历。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's nobody else even remotely close that has achieved and lived through what you've achieved at your age.
zh: 在你这个年纪,取得并经历过你所取得的一切,没有任何人哪怕 remotely 接近。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've read every single book on the history of Facebook.
zh: 我读过关于 Facebook 历史的每一本书。

speaker: Unknown
en: None of them are good.
zh: 没有一本是好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what is missing is this conversation of like how you think about building your business, how you think about building product, how you think about recruiting.
zh: 而缺失的正是这样的对话,比如你如何看待打造你的业务,你如何看待打造产品,你如何看待招聘。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to create the podcast episode that I think is one, desperately needed, and intense, and two, intensely interesting to me.
zh: 我想创造这么一期播客,它一,被迫切需要,而且浓烈,二,对我来说极有兴趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reason I bring that up right now is because this next paragraph goes into this singular experience that Mark Zuckerberg, that is living now, that is operating now at this time in history, has gone through, has experienced.
zh: 我现在提这件事的原因是,下一段将进入 Mark Zuckerberg——那个现在活着、现在正在运转、处在历史这个时点的 Mark Zuckerberg——所经历过的、所体验过的这段独一无二的经历。

speaker: Unknown
en: Listen to this.
zh: 听听这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Zuckerberg achieved his species-warping goal of networking billions of human beings in real-time through social media by age 30.
zh: 扎克伯格在 30 岁前就实现了他那种改变人类物种的目标：通过社交媒体实时连接数十亿人。

speaker: Unknown
en: By 32, he built the most unstoppable entertainment and advertising business in history.
zh: 到 32 岁，他建立了史上最不可阻挡的娱乐和广告业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: By 42, his products are used by one out of every 2.3 people currently breathing.
zh: 到 42 岁，他的产品被当前活着的人口中每 2.3 人中的一人使用。

speaker: Unknown
en: More than the total number of humans that existed in 1965, annual revenue runs well above $200 billion, and Meta's capital expenditure this year will exceed the military budget of every country on Earth except the United States, China, and Russia.
zh: 年收入远超 2000 亿美元，比 1965 年存在于世的全部人类总数还多，而 Meta 今年的资本支出将超过地球上除美国、中国和俄罗斯之外所有国家的军事预算。

speaker: Unknown
en: Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp each have more monthly active users than the number of living adherents to Christianity.
zh: Facebook、Instagram 和 WhatsApp 各自的月活跃用户数都比基督教的现存信徒数量还多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to me this is one of the most important parts.
zh: 而对我来说，这是最重要的部分之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: He is not like the others of his vintage who all at some point abdicate or sell or are overthrown or appoint a regent to face the music instead and recede into varying types of billionaire afterlife.
zh: 他不像他那一辈的其他人——那些人在某个时刻不是退位、出售、被推翻，就是任命一个摄政者代为面对困境，然后隐入各种类型的亿万富翁身后生活。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not for him.
zh: 那不是他的作风。

speaker: Unknown
en: 200 years of peace will not come for free.
zh: 200 年的和平不会是免费的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to do certain things.
zh: 你必须做某些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: You wake up, you hit people, you pay them to hit you.
zh: 你醒来，你打人，你付钱让他们打你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then it's another subpoena and another lawsuit.
zh: 然后又是一张传票，又一场官司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then a product review until 3 a.m.
zh: 然后是一个开到凌晨 3 点的产品评审会。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's another whistleblower with a book deal.
zh: 又有一个告密者签了出书协议。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here comes another Aaron Sorkin movie.
zh: 又一部艾伦·索金的电影要来了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're behind on AI.
zh: 你在 AI 上落后了。

speaker: Unknown
en: No one respects social media.
zh: 没人尊重社交媒体。

speaker: Unknown
en: Testify, pay the settlement, build personal superintelligent, put it in the apps, put it in the sunglasses.
zh: 去作证，支付和解金，构建个人超级智能，把它放进应用里，放进太阳镜里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, that is just incredible writing and an incredible story.
zh: 我的意思是，这真是不可思议的写作和不可思议的故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it goes back to, again, think about the subtitle of this profile, A Journey to the Heart of History's Largest Non-Territorial Empire.
zh: 这又要回到——再次强调——想想这篇人物特写的副标题：通往历史上最大的非领土帝国核心的旅程。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so then Jeremy at this point is at an event for Meta's

zh: 然后她递给 Jeremy 一台笔记本电脑，屏幕上打开的是她女儿的 Google Docs 和 Replit 账户。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Priscilla says, she's quite limited because mom doesn't let her build things on the open internet.
zh: Priscilla 说，她受到很多限制，因为妈妈不让她在开放互联网上构建东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like she wanted to build a dating site.

speaker: Unknown
en: That was a no.
zh: 那被否了。

en: But I wanted to show you some of the things that she has built.

speaker: Unknown
en: We take a look.
zh: 我们来看一看。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a novel she wrote.
zh: 有她写的一本小说。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a blog.
zh: 有一个博客。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a book review of where the mountains meet the moon.
zh: 有一篇《山 meets 月亮》的书评。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are AI-generated motivational theme songs about conquering her fears.
zh: 有关于战胜恐惧的 AI 生成的励志主题歌。

zh: 有一个播客，最新一期的标题是《谈恋爱合不合适？》

speaker: Unknown
en: There is an audiobook library where she narrates books she likes.
zh: 有一个有声书库，她朗读书目里她喜欢的书。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is a Geocities-like website and a Farmville-like game and several apps that she's vibe-coded, including a messaging app.
zh: 有一个类似 Geocities 的网站、一个类似 Farmville 的游戏，还有几个她 vibe coding 出来的应用，包括一个即时通讯应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are business plans for how to market and sell these things.
zh: 还有如何营销和销售这些东西的商业计划。

en: Does Mark have the kids build stuff on computers, I ask?
zh: 我问，Mark 有让孩子们在电脑上构建东西吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: No, she says, he didn't tell her to do any of this.
zh: 她说，没有，这一切他都没有让她去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is she trying to be like her dad, I ask?
zh: 我问，她是在模仿她爸爸吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: No, she says, it's been all on her own.
zh: 她说，没有，这一切完全都是她自己做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is very cute, I respond, but why are you showing me this?
zh: 我回应说，这非常可爱，但你为什么给我看这个？

speaker: Unknown
en: And Priscilla responds, I've known Mark for 23 years.
zh: Priscilla 回答说，我认识 Mark 已经 23 年了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Around year 18 or 19, I said to him, aren't we tired?
zh: 大约在第 18 或 19 年的时候，我对他说，我们是不是累了？

speaker: Unknown
en: Can we be done?
zh: 我们能结束了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm tired.
zh: 我累了。

en: You're tired.
zh: 你也累了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's been a hard run.
zh: 这是一段艰难的历程。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've gotten through a hard chapter.
zh: 我们熬过了一个艰难的篇章。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's call it.
zh: 我们就此收尾吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: There have to be other chapters in our life.
zh: 我们的人生肯定还有别的篇章。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Mark said, no.
zh: 而 Mark 说，不行。

speaker: Unknown
en: He said, no, this is who I am.
zh: 他说，不行，这就是我。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love this.
zh: 我爱这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: I didn't set out to build a company.
zh: 我一开始并不是要创办一家公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just love building things.
zh: 我只是热爱创造东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love being at Meta because I still get to create things.
zh: 我热爱待在 Meta，因为我仍然可以创造东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And until our daughter got a little older, I didn't understand it.
zh: 直到我们女儿长大了一点，我才理解这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now I see her.
zh: 现在我看着她。

speaker: Unknown
en: She just has a desire to build things that is innate, that we didn't teach her.
zh: 她有一种想要创造东西的渴望，那是与生俱来的，不是我们教的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just came.
zh: 它就是这么来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: She's delighted by the idea of bringing something into the world.
zh: 她对把某样东西带到这个世界上的想法感到欣喜。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I tried to take this stuff away from her, it would be like cutting off her arm.
zh: 如果我试图把这些东西从她身边拿走，那就像砍掉她的一条手臂。

speaker: Unknown
en: It wasn't until then that I realized, oh my God, it's Mark.
zh: 直到那时我才意识到，天哪，他就是 Mark。

speaker: Unknown
en: After 23 years, I get it now.
zh: 23 年之后，我现在懂了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't take this away from him.
zh: 你不能把这个从他身上拿走。

speaker: Unknown
en: He wouldn't be him if he stopped.
zh: 如果他停下来，他就不是他了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's the most important line in the profile.
zh: 我认为这是那篇人物专访里最重要的一句话。

en: You can't take this away from him.
zh: 你不能把这个从他身上拿走。

speaker: Unknown
en: He wouldn't be him if he stopped.
zh: 如果他停下来，他就不是他了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that is where I'll leave it.
zh: 我就讲到这里。

en: This is an excellent, excellent profile.
zh: 这是一篇非常、非常出色的人物专访。

speaker: Unknown
en: I hope you read the entire thing.
zh: 我希望你能读完整篇。

speaker: Unknown
en: I will leave a link down in the show notes.
zh: 我会在节目备注里放一个链接。

en: That is 434 books or book length profiles down, 1,000 to go.
zh: 这就是读完的第 434 本书或书长度的专访，还剩 1000 本。

en: And I'll talk to you again soon.
zh: 我们很快再见。
